acceptance.given: Package A changes are proposed against the declared baseline, with the frozen requirements, candidate changes and existing workflow write records available for inspection.

oracle.expected: At planning, authoring, implementation and terminal evaluation, production changes are confined to the eight explicitly declared production paths. Q2 changes are confined to the four declared test modules, skill_quality_support.py and fixtures under scripts/sc/tests/fixtures/skill-quality/; concrete fixture identities are frozen before formal RED. Green/refactor leaves frozen tests and fixtures unchanged. The complete Package A change set and available write records show no protected-path modifications, including transient writes subsequently reverted. Artifact and call-surface inspection finds only the authorized standard, static validator, reference fixtures and migration guidance: no excluded capabilities, permission grants or increase to the user-sandbox tools/network ceiling. Validator and derived evidence contracts retain authorizes=[]. These are boundary assertions attached to compatible foundation/migration verification, not new runtime features or a new evidence system.
forbidden: Production writes outside the eight declared production files.
Q2 production writes, undeclared test/helper/fixture writes, or Green/refactor changes to frozen execution inputs.
Code or test changes to .agents/skills/**, scripts/quick_dev/**, scripts/vdd/** or shared toolchain runtime/evidence writers.
Changes to PhaseA.Platform/**, PhaseA.Platform.Tests/**, runtime/**, live metadata, hosted workspaces, Phase authentication/authorization or the Runner.
Changes to scripts/sc/_llm_backend.py, model-routing policy or shared Codex entrypoints.
Changes to knowledge publication, Skill-input authority/generation stores, 7-31, TC-D2--TC-D6, BMAD/VDD knowledge-query behavior, S1/S2/S3 or app-server/SDK.
Rewriting or deleting historical Bootstrap, TDD, acceptance, freeze or implementation reports.

Adding OIDC, a total-entry Skill, physical user deletion, user-installed MCP, platform telemetry, a new error ledger, a second validation evidence system, Godot runtime analysis, package installation or mandatory internal review.
Raising the user-sandbox tools/network ceiling or treating static validation as execution authorization.
Inferring scope compliance solely from validator return values, a clean final diff, command invocation or a historical status.
oracle.observable: During planning and terminal boundary evaluation, compare declared owner/write/snapshot sets, complete candidate changes and existing workflow write records against frozen NFR-1/NFR-2 boundaries; inspect changed normative artifacts, validator call surfaces and tests for excluded functionality or expanded authority.

acceptance.then: Package A changes and tests remain within their declared authorization boundary; protected paths remain untouched, excluded capabilities are absent, and the user-sandbox tools/network ceiling is unchanged.
acceptance.when: The candidate write contract is checked before authoring, stage write records are checked after authoring and implementation, and the complete candidate is evaluated at whole-plan terminal validation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Attach explicit scope assertions to the declared foundation artifact checks and migration terminal context, including scripts/sc/tests/test_skill_quality_migration.py::test_a24. Inspect the complete candidate write set, existing stage write records, changed normative artifacts and real validator call surfaces. Raise AssertionError for an unauthorized production/test write, protected-path modification, excluded capability or increased sandbox authority. Preserve a separate boundary oracle; validator pass status cannot discharge it. Use the declared whole-plan pytest argv with a caller-enforced 600-second timeout after all four modules are authored and their behaviors exercised. This constraint is a non-RED artifact guard, not an expected-red runtime marker. Missing modules, unavailable write records, collection errors and timeouts are validation gaps or harness failures, never successful boundary proof or causal product RED.

affected_subjects: Package A scope and write authorization
Protected toolchain, Phase, runtime, shared LLM, knowledge and historical evidence
slice_hint.behavior_change: Constrain the compatible Package A foundation, declaration, capability and migration work to the frozen production and Q2 boundaries. Add explicit boundary assertions in the declared test context without implementing a new controller, runtime feature or evidence writer.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert only attributable Package A production changes while preserving user changes, frozen execution inputs and historical failure evidence. Preserve existing Skill contract protocols and all toolchain, Phase, runtime and sandbox authority. No live database migration or runtime-state mutation is authorized.

slice_hint.state_transition: Package A work is proposed against the frozen scope; planning, stage and terminal checks establish whether its writes and capabilities stayed inside that scope. Any violation blocks closure and requires bounded repair without expanding authorization.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: All five scope assertions have current artifact/boundary proof, not merely runtime return values. Stage records and complete candidate changes establish the production/Q2 partition and protected-path preservation; artifact/call-surface checks establish excluded-capability absence and unchanged sandbox authority. Run the declared four-module terminal selection once all required tests are authored and behaviors exercised, with a 600-second timeout; targeted current/predecessor checks use exact applicable node IDs and 300-second timeouts. Retain failures, invalidate affected proofs after shared production changes and rebuild the original binding identity before replaying with that same identity. No protected controller changes, fabricated receipts or independent guard implementation slice are authorized. Missing first-use production binding, required sources or boundary evidence blocks the applicable check rather than manufacturing RED or claiming completion.
